claims.text: This dispute concerns one trip on every record before the tribunal: EV-TRIP-00512, EV-GPS-00512 and EV-FARE-00512 each carry trip_id TRP-00512, and the trace's first fix at 19:16:40 matches the trip_record's started_at of 19:16:40. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) — that the artifacts describe the same trip — is therefore met on the face of the bundle. (EV-GPS-00512 is impaired: issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE, weight_multiplier 0.39; I disclose that impairment in every claim that cites it.)

The excess is established on the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 8.92 km against a booked optimal of 6.1 km, giving an excess of 2.82 km and 46.23% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass — the absolute gate is 'greater than 0.8 km' and the proportional gate is 'greater than 20%' — and POL-RD-01 expressly directs that trace_distance_km governs over the rounded convenience copy trip_record.actual_distance_km of 8.9 km, which may not be cited for the threshold test. (EV-GPS-00512 impaired — GPS_GAP, LOW_COVERAGE, weight 0.39.)

Even on the reading most favourable to the driver, the impairment does not dissolve the excess. Under POL-RD-07(i) the impaired stretch is measured as the straight line between its bounding fixes precisely to favour the driver, and on that measurement the deviation still records 2.82 km of excess — the gap narrows the measurement, it does not erase it. (EV-GPS-00512 impaired — GPS_GAP with a 860 s gap and LOW_COVERAGE at 44.9%, weight 0.39.)

The independent corroboration POL-RD-07(ii) requires to carry an impaired trace is present, and it comes from the driver himself: his counterparty statement says 'My phone hung, so I drove from memory', which is a counterparty_statement admitting the route actually driven was not the platform's optimal route, and it is sourced outside the trace entirely. EV-TRIP-00512 supplies the booked optimal of 6.1 km against which that admission is measured. (EV-GPS-00512 cited and impaired — GPS_GAP, LOW_COVERAGE, weight 0.39.)

No closure exoneration is available on this record. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00512-01, is MISSING: no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window, its weight is 0.0 and it carries no payload. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run, and not one metre of the 2.82 km excess is exonerated. The absence is itself citable, and I cite it.

Nor is there a rider-requested detour to exonerate anything. EV-CHAT-00512 records message_count 0 with an empty message array, so there is no rider instruction, timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor or within three minutes after, and no waypoint_hint from which POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test could be run. The driver's claim that the rider caused the detour has no artifact behind it.

No relocation adjustment can reduce the baseline either. EV-TRIP-00512 shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so there is no amended re-quote for POL-RD-05 to apply, and the booked optimal of 6.1 km stands as the comparator for the excess.

The driver's explanation — that his phone hung — is a general assertion pointing to no artifact and no clause. POL-RD-08 shifts the burden to the driver to identify a specific artifact and a specific clause, and provides that unsupported assertions carry no weight; the empty chat log EV-CHAT-00512 leaves his account uncorroborated on the record, while the trace's 8.92 km stands against him.

On the POL-RD-02 arithmetic the refund comes to SGD 6.35: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 6.1 optimal km + 0.28 x 11.0 optimal min) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 12.255, and the refund is charged_total 18.56 less 12.255 = 6.305, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05.

That refund is neither de minimis nor near-total, so the outcome is a partial refund and not NO_ACTION: 6.305 is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor in POL-RD-02, and it is 33.97% of charged_total, far below the 90% share that would convert it into a FULL_REFUND. The rider is entitled to SGD 6.35 back and to have the remaining charge recomputed on the optimal route rather than the route the driver chose.

The excess is if anything understated rather than inflated. EV-TRIP-00512 records the dropoff as 'Serangoon Ave 2, 600 m short of Blk 231' because the driver ended the trip early, so the 8.92 km trace is a floor on the distance actually driven and the 2.82 km excess measured from it cannot be an artefact of over-counting distance.

The rider's own profile gives the tribunal no basis to demand corroboration beyond the trace. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so POL-RD-08's enhanced-corroboration condition — four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated — is not met on any reading; and in any event the condition speaks to sub-30% claims, while the excess here is 46.23%.

If the judge concludes the driver's statement does not corroborate the trace, the case still cannot end in a ruling that leaves this rider carrying the disputed charge. POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) make ESCALATE mandatory where a trace impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) has no independent corroboration, and POL-GEN-03 provides that an escalated amount is held rather than collected. Either way the rider is not left paying for a route that was not hers. (EV-GPS-00512 is impaired — GPS_GAP, LOW_COVERAGE, weight 0.39.)

claims.text: The GPS trace for this trip is impaired for policy purposes, not merely down-weighted at schema level. It contains a single 860-second gap between consecutive fixes (19:23:30 to 19:37:50) — far beyond the 90-second limb (a) of POL-RD-07 — and covers only 44.9% of the active window. The admissibility pre-pass tags it IMPAIRED at weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE, and I disclose that impairment, weight and those issue codes here, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires of any advocate relying on it.

Because the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), POL-RD-07(ii) forbids establishing a deviation on the gps_trace alone. The whole 2.82 km excess here is the trace distance of 8.92 km less the booked optimal of 6.1 km: the deciding fact is carried by the impaired trace (EV-GPS-00512, weight 0.39, issues GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE) and by nothing else, and the trip record's 8.9 km is only the rounded convenience copy POL-RD-01 tells the tribunal not to cite for the threshold test.

None of the independent sources POL-RD-07(ii) names exists on this record. The chat log holds zero messages, so there is no driver admission in it; the fare breakdown charges no ERP gantry at all (erp_gantries is empty, tolls 0.00), so no gantry places the vehicle on any corridor the optimal route avoids; and the billed 8.9 km is a copy of the same impaired trace measurement of 8.92 km (EV-GPS-00512, weight 0.39, issues GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE), which POL-RD-01 says governs the measurement and POL-RD-07(ii) expressly refuses to treat as independent corroboration.

The driver's counterparty statement does not fill that gap either. It explains that his phone hung, that he drove from memory and that he ended the trip before her block; it names no road, corridor or waypoint, and the trip record agrees only that the dropoff was some 600 m short of Blk 231. That is not 'a counterparty_statement admitting the route' as POL-RD-07(ii) requires — at its highest it admits a lost navigation aid, not any identified trajectory — so it cannot carry the 2.82 km excess across the 860-second gap in the impaired trace (EV-GPS-00512, weight 0.39, issues GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE).

It follows that POL-RD-10(3) is engaged: the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) (one 860-second gap, under 45% coverage — EV-GPS-00512 at weight 0.39, issues GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE) and no corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names exists. The case must not receive a final ruling; it escalates to a human reviewer with both briefs and the admissibility report, and that escalation is terminal — the disputed 18.56 is held, not collected or refunded.

Independently of POL-RD-10(3), the confidence cap in POL-GEN-02(2) sits below the platform floor. The deciding fact — the excess — is carried solely by the impaired trace at weight 0.39 (issues GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE), because the trip record's 8.9 km and the ledger's billed distance are both copies of that same trace measurement rather than independent carriers. A cap of 0.39 is below the 0.70 floor, so POL-RD-10(1) escalates this case in any event.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and cannot discharge it. Limb (b) requires an excess measured from an unimpaired trace, or — where the trace is impaired — from an independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii). The trace here is impaired (EV-GPS-00512, weight 0.39, issues GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE) and there is no such independent source anywhere in the pool. Her claim is therefore not sustained on the present record, and under POL-RD-07(iii) the consequence of that evidential failure is escalation, not a finding against the driver.

Even taken at its highest, the excess is not a material deviation, so POL-RD-06's driver-profile check is not triggered: 2.82 km is 46.2% of the 6.1 km optimal, under the 50% gate, and far under the 8.0 km absolute gate. If the profile were consulted it would find nothing against this driver — deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in the last 90 days — so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor the conduct referral in POL-RD-06 is available on this record, and the trace relied on for the figure is itself impaired at weight 0.39 with issues GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

There is no billing-integrity correction owing under POL-RD-09: the ledger carries no ERP lines, no tolls, no airport surcharge and a zero cancellation fee, so there is no phantom gantry or wrongly applied surcharge to refund in full as a standalone correction that would survive even a failed deviation claim. The only money the rider seeks is a distance-and-time refund, and that route is closed while the trace is impaired (EV-GPS-00512, weight 0.39, issues GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE).

The traffic-advisory artifact for this trip is MISSING — weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload — so the pool contains no evidence of the conditions on the optimal corridor and POL-RD-03 cannot be run for either party. Absence is itself citable, and it means the corridor state is simply unknown here: that is a data gap, and POL-RD-10 treats data gaps as grounds for a human reviewer rather than as findings against the driver.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this case cannot be decided on the present record, and I am escalating it. Here is why, and what would settle it.

The trip itself is not in dispute. EV-TRIP-00512, EV-GPS-00512 and EV-FARE-00512 all carry trip TRP-00512, and the trace's first fix at 19:16:40 matches the trip record's started_at of 19:16:40, so the rider's identification burden under POL-RD-08(a) is met.

The difficulty is the route evidence. EV-GPS-00512 is impaired both at schema level and for policy purposes: it contains a single 860-second gap between consecutive fixes (19:23:30 to 19:37:50) — fourteen minutes of a twenty-six-minute trip — and covers only 44.9% of the active window, and the pre-pass tags it GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE at weight 0.39. A gap of more than 90 seconds is limb (a) of POL-RD-07, so the trace is impaired for policy purposes and not merely down-weighted at schema level; both things are true and I say both.

On the trace's own figure the rider's arithmetic is correct: trace_distance_km 8.92 less the booked optimal_distance_km 6.1 gives an excess of 2.82 km, 46.2% of optimal, passing both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%). But POL-RD-07(ii) forbids establishing a deviation on the impaired trace alone and requires an independent source.

No such source exists. EV-CHAT-00512 holds zero messages, so there is no driver admission in the chat log. The fare breakdown charges no ERP gantry and no toll (erp_gantries empty, tolls 0.00), so no gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route avoids. The billed 8.9 km is a rounded copy of the same trace measurement, which POL-RD-01 says governs for the threshold test and POL-RD-07(ii) expressly refuses as independent corroboration.
